scenes.label: Meet Tara
scenes.title: Dusty’s big day
scenes.caption: Meet Tara. Her class built a robot cleaner called Dusty, and she's writing its program for Open Day. Move right, sweep. Move right, sweep. She copies the same two lines again and again, one pair for each tile in the row. The list keeps growing, and she's proud of it.
scenes.dialogue: Dusty will make our lab shine on Open Day!

scenes.label: The bump
scenes.title: Bump! Right into the bin.
scenes.caption: At the test run, Dusty sweeps every tile, then rolls on and bumps into the bin! Scraps spill across the floor. Tara's cheeks go hot, and Open Day is tomorrow. Somewhere in her long list is one extra pair. But the list is so long, she can't spot it.
scenes.dialogue: Oh no! Which line did I get wrong?

scenes.label: Ask Mr Rao
scenes.title: Say it once. Say how many.
scenes.caption: Mr Rao, the lab teacher, sits beside her. Copy slips happen to every coder. Together they count: six pairs, but only five tiles. “When steps repeat,” he says, “write them once, and say how many times.” This is called a loop. Her list could shrink to three lines.
scenes.speech: Mister Rao, the lab teacher, sits beside her. Copy slips happen to every coder. Together they count: six pairs, but only five tiles. “When steps repeat,” he says, “write them once, and say how many times.” This is called a loop. Her list could shrink to three lines.
scenes.dialogue: So I write it once, then count once?

scenes.label: Build the loop
scenes.title: Build the loop. Count it right.
scenes.caption: Your turn. Help Tara build the loop. First, choose the steps that repeat. Then set the count: one repeat for each tile. Run it and watch Dusty. With the wrong count, Dusty stops short or bumps the bin again. Count the tiles carefully!
scenes.dialogue: One repeat for every tile. Let’s count!

scenes.label: Why loops win
scenes.title: Shorter, clearer, easier to change.
scenes.caption: REPEAT 5 TIMES: Dusty cleans every tile and stops right before the bin. Three lines now replace her long list. A loop is easier to read, easier to check, and easier to change. If the row grows to eight tiles, Tara changes just one number. The count must match the work.
scenes.speech: Repeat five times: Dusty cleans every tile and stops right before the bin. Three lines now replace her long list. A loop is easier to read, easier to check, and easier to change. If the row grows to eight tiles, Tara changes just one number. The count must match the work.
scenes.dialogue: Three lines, and not a single copy slip!

scenes.label: Open Day
scenes.title: One small card. One clean row.
scenes.caption: Open Day! Dusty rolls down the row, sweeps each tile, and stops neatly before the bin. The parents clap, and Tara beams. Her program now fits on one small card. A loop says it once, with the right count. Your turn: help Tara inspect more robot programs!
scenes.dialogue: Dusty did it, and my code fits on a card!
